title: A modified high-throughput analysis of PLFAs in soil
author: Ellis, Ritz
materials: The following is provided as an indicative set-up and procedure.1Inject 1 μl of sample into the GC, ensuring that the GC is set to split-less mode.2The column used in our work is a ZB-FFAP, supplied by Phenomenex® (Macclesfield, UK). It is 30 m in length, with 0.25 mm inner diameter and 0.25 μm film thickness. Helium is used as a carrier gas, with a constant pressure of 18 psi. Initial oven temperature is 120 °C that is maintained for 1 min. The machine is programmed to increase in temperature (5 °C/minute) to 250 °C. This temperature (250 °C) is then maintained throughout the run.3The results are displayed as a chromatogram, showing the retention times of each compound. Xcalibur® (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, US) is used to obtain and identify the PLFAs within each sample. The mass spectroscopy provides the ion profile of each compound, which aids in the identification of the peaks when compared to the internal and external standards.

steps.title: Freeze and freeze‑dry soil
steps.instruction: Place freshly sampled soil in a –80 °C freezer immediately, then freeze‑dry it and determine the dry weight.

steps.title: Weigh soil and include blanks
steps.instruction: Weigh 2–3 g of the freeze‑dried soil into a 13 mm × 100 mm glass screw‑cap test tube; include 1–2 blank tubes.

steps.title: Add Bligh‑Dyer extractant
steps.instruction: Add 4.0 ml of Bligh‑Dyer extractant to each tube.

steps.title: Seal and hand‑shake tubes
steps.instruction: Seal the tubes with Teflon‑lined screw‑cap lids and shake by hand until the extractant and soil are well mixed.

steps.title: Sonicate samples
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in an ultrasonic bath at room temperature and sonicate for 10 min, ensuring tubes are not packed too closely.

steps.title: End‑over‑end shaking
steps.instruction: Shake the sealed tubes on an end‑over‑end shaker for 2 h.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 10 min at 1500 rpm to separate liquid and solid phases; if any soil re‑suspends, centrifuge again before proceeding.

substeps.instruction: If using the same centrifugal evaporator for this step, keep the vacuum pump turned off.

steps.title: Transfer liquid phase
steps.instruction: Using a fresh glass pipette with a fresh rubber bulb for each sample, transfer the liquid phase to a clean 13 mm × 100 mm glass screw‑cap tube with a Teflon‑lined lid.

substeps.instruction: Replace the rubber bulb for each extraction run or whenever it becomes visibly contaminated.

steps.title: Add chloroform and water
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml chloroform and 1 ml de‑ionised water (diH₂O or Milli‑Q) to each tube and reseal.

steps.title: Vortex and second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube for 5 s, then centrifuge at 1500 rpm for 10 min to separate the two liquid phases.

substeps.instruction: If using the same centrifugal evaporator, keep the vacuum pump off.

steps.title: Remove upper phase and particles
steps.instruction: Using a glass pipette with a rubber bulb, discard the upper phase (and any visible particles) into appropriate waste.

steps.title: Evaporate lower phase
steps.instruction: Evaporate the remaining lower phase at 30 °C for 40 min in a centrifugal evaporator (miVac Duo Concentrator, pump, Speed Trap, rotor DRC‑13100‑032, GeneVac, UK) under vacuum.

substeps.instruction: If nitrogen evaporation is used instead, direct a nitrogen stream over the meniscus sufficient to disrupt the surface without splash‑back, adjusting the flow as the volume decreases.

steps.title: Store dried extracts
steps.instruction: Store the dried extracts at –20 °C overnight or until ready for GC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Inject sample into GC
steps.instruction: Inject 1 µl of the sample into the gas chromatograph in split‑less mode.

steps.title: Set GC column and temperature program
steps.instruction: Use a ZB‑FFAP column (30 m × 0.25 mm ID, 0.25 µm film, Phenomenex); helium carrier gas at constant 18 psi; oven 120 °C (hold 1 min), ramp 5 °C/min to 250 °C, hold 250 °C for the remainder of the run.

steps.title: Acquire and identify PLFA data
steps.instruction: Collect the chromatogram with Xcalibur (Thermo Fisher); identify PLFAs using the mass‑spectral ion profile compared to internal and external standards.

description: 1All drying and evaporation steps should be performed in vacuo, using a centrifugal evaporator (with vacuum pump and cold trap). Where possible, all centrifugation steps should use the same centrifugal evaporator but with the vacuum pump turned off.2Evaporation under nitrogen can be used instead of a centrifugal evaporator [2]. If nitrogen evaporation is to be substituted, ensure that the flow of nitrogen over the meniscus of the sample is enough to cause disruption of the entire surface (but not to cause splash-back). This will ensure that all of the air is displaced from the surface of the sample, diminishing degradation of the sample. The stream of nitrogen (or placement) may also need to be altered during evaporation as the sample reduces in volume.3Specified 13 mm by 100 mm glass screw-cap test tubes are used throughout as they match the rotor (DRC-13100-032) for the miVac Centrifugal Concentrator. Approximately 30 samples and 2 blanks can be processed simultaneously with this rotor. When procuring such test tubes, some of them may not be of consistent size and will therefore not fit into the specified rotor. These can be used in the first step where Bligh-Dyer extractant is added, as an alternate centrifuge can be used with less strict constraints. There may be cheaper glass alternatives if using a different machine or using nitrogen evaporation. Additionally, for the last step, 13 mm by 100 mm rimless glass test tubes may be better to use as the diameter of the screw-cap variety can prevent the insertion of an electronic pipette. If using an electronic pipette to transfer the sample to the amber vial from a screw-cap test tube, the tip ejector arm of the pipette may need to be removed in order to fit.4Within this method, Teflon lined lids were used throughout. This was to prevent plasticide contamination. These have a finite usage and must be cleaned appropriately if re-used.
